key_insight: A new nonlinear time-domain potential-flow model offers an efficient framework for predicting wave scattering by a surface-piercing cylinder.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports wave-load analysis for large-diameter offshore structures such as wind-turbine monopiles and platform columns.
method: Represent nonlinear wave evolution with a time-domain pseudo-spectral model.
Use a second-kind Fredholm integral equation and Legendre polynomials.
Solve for cylinder-surface velocity potential and free-surface vertical velocity.
evidence_signal: Verification compares small-steepness uniform-wave scattering against a direct Fourier-transform approach and established theoretical models, with convergence and computational efficiency also demonstrated.
watch_item: Validation for highly nonlinear transient waves is deferred to Part II; this is a potential-flow solver, not an AI or turbulence model.
paper_title: On Modelling the Scattering of Highly Nonlinear Transient Water Waves Due to Surface-Piercing Cylinder. Part I: Formulations and Verifications
